 {"content": "# Workflow: Club Representative Appeal & Dispute\n\nEnd-to-end process for raising, reviewing, and resolving a result or standing\ndispute submitted by a club representative.\n\nThis workflow is intentionally a thin, requester-facing wrapper around\n`WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md`, which is the canonical exception engine.\nDo not duplicate full exception mechanics here; use this workflow to describe\nclub-entry and follow-up touchpoints only.\n\n## Overview\n\nWhen a club representative believes a match result is incorrect or that a ruling\nwas applied unfairly, they can raise a formal dispute. The dispute is captured as\na `federation.override_request` and goes through the governance review pipeline.\nThe outcome may be a result correction, a sanction reduction, a standing\nadjustment, or a formal rejection with reasons.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Override requests, decisions, audit notes, outcomes |\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Result correction after approved override |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standing adjustment after result correction |\n| `sports_federation_portal` | Club representative raises appeal via portal or back-office |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Notifications to all parties at key decision points |\n| `sports_federation_base` | Core club / match records referenced by the request |\n| `mail` | Chatter audit trail on the override request |\n\n## Models\n\n| Model | Key Fields |\n|-------|-----------|\n| `federation.override.request` | `title`, `request_type`, `target_model`, `target_res_id`, `reason`, `state`, `requester_id`, `decision_note`, `implementation_note` |\n\n## Override Request Types relevant to appeals\n\n| Type | Use case |\n|------|---------|\n| `result_correction` | Incorrect score, forfeit dispute, missing goal |\n| `standing_adjustment` | Points awarded incorrectly; does not require score change |\n| `eligibility_waiver` | Player ruled ineligible unfairly |\n| `sanction_reduction` | Disciplinary fine or suspension reduction request |\n\n## State Machine\n\n```\ndraft → submitted → approved → implemented → closed\n                 ↘ rejected  → closed\n      ← withdrawn (submitted → draft)\n```\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Club Representative Raises a Dispute\n\n**Actor**: Club representative\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance` (via portal or back office)\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Governance → Override Requests** (back office) or\n   the portal appeal section (if enabled).\n2. Click **New** and fill in:\n   - **Title** — clear one-line description of the dispute\n   - **Request Type** — e.g. `result_correction`\n   - **Target Record** — the match, result, or standing being disputed (set\n     `target_model` and `target_res_id`)\n   - **Reason** — full factual justification\n3. Save in `draft` state. Add supporting attachments via the chatter.\n4. Click **Submit** when ready: `draft → submitted`.\n\nThe requester and request timestamp are recorded automatically.\n\n**Withdrawal**: if the club needs to amend the request before a decision is\nmade, click **Withdraw** to return from `submitted → draft`, edit, and resubmit.\n\n### 2. Federation Staff Governance Review\n\n**Actor**: Governance officer\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\n1. Open the submitted request from\n   **Federation → Governance → Override Requests → Submitted**.\n2. Review the request, target record, and any supporting attachments.\n3. Use the chatter to request clarification from the club if needed (keeps a\n   timestamped record).\n4. Add **Audit Notes** for internal commentary that should not be visible to\n   the club representative.\n\nThere is no separate `under_review` state. Operational review happens while the\nrequest remains in `submitted` state.\n\n### 3. Decision Recording\n\n**Actor**: Governance officer\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\nAfter review, the governance officer decides:\n\n- **Approve**: `submitted → approved`\n  - Add a `decision_note` explaining the basis for approval.\n  - The standard approve action creates a decision record automatically.\n- **Reject**: `submitted → rejected`\n  - Add a `decision_note` with the rejection reason.\n  - The club representative is notified (if notifications module is installed).\n\nThe governance officer records only the decision — implementation is handled\nseparately to keep the audit trail clean.\n\n### 4. Decision Notification\n\n**Actor**: System\n**Module**: `sports_federation_notifications`\n\nOn state transition to `approved` or `rejected`:\n\n- The club representative (requester) receives a notification with the decision\n  and the `decision_note`.\n- The federation manager group receives a notification for `approved` requests\n  that require implementation.\n\n### 5. Outcome Implementation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance` + affected owning module\n\nIf approved:\n\n| Request Type | Implementation Action |\n|---|---|\n| `result_correction` | Update `home_score` / `away_score` on the match; re-run result approval pipeline |\n| `standing_adjustment` | Unfreeze standings if frozen; manually adjust; re-freeze |\n| `eligibility_waiver` | Create or reinstate player license; update roster line |\n| `sanction_reduction` | Edit disciplinary sanction amount or suspension length |\n\nSteps:\n1. Open the approved override request.\n2. Implement the correction in the relevant module (see table above).\n3. Record what was done in `implementation_note` on the request form.\n4. Click **Mark Implemented**: `approved → implemented`.\n5. An outcome-log row is written automatically so later review can see what was\n   done, not just what was approved.\n\n### 6. Closure\n\n**Actor**: Governance officer or federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_governance`\n\nOnce all follow-up is complete:\n\n1. Open the `implemented` or `rejected` request.\n2. Click **Close**: state → `closed`.\n3. Only `implemented` or `rejected` requests can be closed.\n4. Closed requests are read-only and permanently preserved in the audit trail.\n\n## Audit Trail\n\nThe complete audit trail includes:\n\n- Request creation with requester and timestamp\n- Submission and any withdrawal back to draft (with timestamps)\n- Decision (approve / reject) with decision note and officer identity\n- Implementation note describing what was done\n- Closure timestamp\n\nAll state transitions are logged in the chatter via `mail.tracking.value`.\n\n## Impact on Standings\n\nFor result corrections that change scores:\n\n1. Corrected result re-enters the approval pipeline: the administrator re-submits\n   and re-approves the result.\n2. Standings in `draft` or `ready` state recompute automatically.\n3. If standings are `frozen`, the administrator must unfreeze → recompute →\n   re-freeze (see [WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md](WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md)).\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md](WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md) — Generic override request process for all exception types.\n- [WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — Result approval and re-approval after correction.\n- [WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md](WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md) — Freeze / unfreeze and recompute steps.\n\nUnified operator model reminder:\n\n- Raise dispute/request exception on the owning record.\n- Resolve through Governance Override.\n- Re-run result approval and standings publication recovery where needed.\n", "content_length": 7409, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "063f3e885e799adca4fdff955d7222fbc4332d02038b775bc52176ca5601c251", "size_bytes": 7467}
 {"content": "# Workflow: Club Onboarding\n\nEnd-to-end process for registering a new club with the federation — from initial\nrequest through compliance document intake, bank-details entry, first-season\nregistration, and portal access grant.\n\n## Overview\n\nA new club must be formally onboarded before it can enter teams in tournaments.\nOnboarding spans four areas: master-data setup, compliance document collection,\nfinance details, and portal access for the club representative. These steps can\nrun partly in parallel once the club record exists.\n\nUse this workflow as the primary new-club journey. Compliance, finance, and\nseason-registration workflows support it, but they should not be presented as\nseparate equal-weight starting points when staff are onboarding a brand-new\nclub.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Club, team, and season master data |\n| `sports_federation_compliance` | Document requirement tracking |\n| `sports_federation_portal` | Club representative portal access |\n| `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | Bank details, registration fee event |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Welcome and missing-document notifications |\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. New Club Request\n\n**Actor**: Club applicant (off-system) → Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_base`\n\nThe federation receives a new-club application through its standard intake\nchannel (email, paper form, or future portal form). The federation administrator\ncreates the club record:\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Configuration → Clubs** and click **New**.\n2. Fill in:\n   - **Name** — official club name\n   - **Code** — short unique code (e.g. `MFC`)\n   - **Email**, **Phone**, **Website** (optional)\n   - **Address** — postal address for correspondence\n3. Save. The club starts with `active = True` and no additional state.\n\nAt this point the club exists in the system but is not yet enrolled in any season\nand has no compliance documents or portal access.\n\n### 2. Federation Staff Review\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_base` + `sports_federation_compliance`\n\nBefore proceeding with compliance intake, the administrator performs a background\nreview:\n\n- Verify the club is not a duplicate (search by name and code).\n- Confirm the founding documents meet federation bylaws.\n- Confirm at least one responsible contact person has been nominated.\n\nNo formal review state exists on the club record itself. Use the chatter\n(Discuss tab on the club form) to record review notes.\n\n### 3. Compliance Document Intake\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator or club contact\n**Module**: `sports_federation_compliance`\n\nCreate one `federation.compliance.submission` per document requirement that\napplies to clubs (`required_for_all = True` for the `club` target model):\n\nCommon requirements at onboarding:\n\n| Requirement | Expiry? | Notes |\n|------------|---------|-------|\n| Public Liability Insurance | Yes (annual) | Minimum coverage amount per federation rules |\n| Club Registration Certificate | No | Official registration with national authority |\n| Bank Account Confirmation Letter | No | Matches bank details to be entered |\n| Club Rules & Constitution | No | Signed copy |\n\nFor each document:\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Compliance → Document Submissions**.\n2. Create a submission linked to the club and the relevant requirement.\n3. Attach the scanned or PDF document.\n4. Submit: state `draft → submitted`.\n5. The compliance officer reviews and approves: state `submitted → approved`.\n\nIf `sports_federation_notifications` is installed, an approval confirmation is\nsent to the club contact on each approval.\n\n### 4. Bank Details Entry\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_finance_bridge`\n\n1. Evidence is written under\n`artifacts/release/migration/` by default.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n- production-like database and filestore restore;\n- pre-upgrade invariant snapshot;\n- reviewed module upgrade;\n- post-upgrade invariant comparison;\n- role-separated operator pilot;\n- backup checksum and restore evidence;\n- rollback drill with named owner and trigger;\n- archived RC logs and machine-readable evidence.\n\n### Exit criteria\n\nThe upgraded copy preserves competition, registration, fixture, schedule,\npublication, match-day, result, standings, portal, public, integration, and\nattachment invariants. Restore and rollback complete from the recorded backup.\n\n## Simplified Competition Journey\n\nStatus: **Implemented**\n\n### Objective\n\nAllow a normal league, tournament day, or cup to be configured, scheduled,\napproved, and published without exposing the underlying Odoo model structure.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n- template-led competition creation;\n- guided Basics, Participants, Format, Calendar, Schedule, Publish journey;\n- user-facing Draft, Ready, Live, Finished presentation states;\n- visible blockers, responsible role, and next action;\n- advanced stage graph, revision, fairness, and shared-day controls separated\n  from the normal path;\n- task-first club portal.\n\n### Reversibility contract\n\n- Setup templates apply editable defaults and can be cancelled.\n- Late fixtures can be added to or removed from calendar allocations.\n- Draft and change-requested schedules refresh from the current calendar plan without deleting assignments.\n- Submitting planners can withdraw pending reviews; approver-requested changes return the same schedule to an editable state.\n- Published evidence stays immutable and corrections use a linked replacement revision.\n\n### Exit criteria\n\nA trained non-developer completes the normal journey without developer mode, direct model navigation, manual progression mapping, or shell access. Every pre-publication handoff has an explicit return path; post-publication changes use traceable replacement revisions.\n\n## Operational Job Reliability\n\nStatus: **Implemented**\n\n### Objective\n\nGeneralize the proven standings recompute reliability pattern without moving\ndomain execution out of its owning addon.\n\n### Deliverables\n\n- bounded retry and backoff;\n- stale-running recovery;\n- dead-letter/operator-action state;\n- correlation IDs and sanitized error evidence;\n- idempotent manual retry;\n- operator visibility for notification, report, integration, retention, and\n  snapshot jobs;\n- shared infrastructure only after two proven consumers exist.\n\n### Implementation\n\nThe shared `federation.operation.job` queue records source ownership, attempts,\nretry timing, correlation IDs, stale-worker recovery, terminal operator action,\nand manual retry. Notification and scheduled-report failures can be queued for\nautomatic retry. Failed inbound deliveries create operator-action jobs because\npayload and governance corrections require explicit review before replay.\n\nThe **Operational Job Health** administration view groups  {"content": "# Competition Workflow Ownership\n\nThe ownership chain is the supported competition-planning architecture. No\nproduction data migration is required solely for this ownership clarification.\n\n## Capability ownership\n\n- Competition Core owns edition lifecycle and role assignments.\n- Registration owns entries and versioned finalized participant sets.\n- Format Studio owns stage topology, logical fixtures, standings snapshots, and progression.\n- Calendar owns physical match days, courts, and availability slots.\n- Scheduling owns fixture-to-slot assignments and fairness proposals.\n- Schedule Approval owns independent review and immutable publications.\n- Result Control owns the complete result lifecycle.\n- Match-Day Operations owns live execution and incidents.\n\n## Domain event contract\n\nEvents are past-tense facts. Producers emit only after a successful state change. Consumers must be idempotent and may not mutate the producer aggregate. Event payloads contain stable record IDs, version/revision, actor, and reason where applicable.\n\nRequired events: participant_set_finalized, structure_frozen, stage_standings_frozen, stage_progression_applied, matchday_capacity_ready, schedule_submitted, schedule_approved, schedule_published, matchday_opened, result_approved, result_contested, result_corrected, matchday_closed.\n", "content_length": 1325, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "docs/competition_engine_ownership.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3352ecae7e79ab9a7fa5079eca2e62c212b65a59136effde4e6945b21563894c", "size_bytes": 1325}

 {"content": "Sports Federation Compliance\n============================\n\nDocument requirements, submissions, and compliance checking. Ensures that\nclubs, players, referees, and venues maintain all required documentation\n(licenses, insurance certificates, safety reports, and similar evidence).\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nDefines what **documents are required** for each entity type, tracks\n**submissions** with attachments and expiry dates, and runs\n**compliance checks** to flag missing or expired documentation.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_base``: Clubs.\n- ``sports_federation_people``: Players.\n- ``sports_federation_officiating``: Referees.\n- ``sports_federation_venues``: Venues.\n- ``sports_federation_portal``: Club representatives.\n- ``mail``: Chatter.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.document.requirement``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA type of document that certain entities must provide.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Requirement title.\n- ``code`` (Char): Unique code.\n- ``target_model`` (Selection): Entity type such as club, player, referee,\n   venue, or club representative.\n- ``required_for_all`` (Boolean): Applies to all entities of that type.\n- ``requires_expiry_date`` (Boolean): Submission must include an expiry date.\n- ``validity_days`` (Integer): Default validity period.\n- ``description`` (Text): Detailed requirements.\n- ``active`` (Boolean): Whether the requirement is currently enforced.\n\n``federation.document.submission``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nAn actual document submitted against a requirement.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Submission title.\n- ``requirement_id`` (Many2one): Requirement being fulfilled.\n- ``target_model`` (Selection, computed): Copied from the requirement.\n- ``club_id`` / ``player_id`` / ``referee_id`` / ``venue_id`` /\n   ``club_representative_id`` (Many2one): Target entity.\n- ``status`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``submitted``, ``approved``,\n   ``rejected``, ``replacement_requested``, or ``expired``.\n- ``attachment_ids`` (Many2many): Uploaded files.\n- ``issue_date`` / ``expiry_date`` (Date): Document validity.\n- ``reviewer_id`` (Many2one): Reviewer.\n- ``reviewed_on`` (Datetime): Review timestamp.\n- ``is_expired`` (Boolean, computed): True when ``expiry_date`` is before\n   today.\n- ``target_display`` (Char, computed): Readable target entity name.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\n- **State machine**: ``draft -> submitted -> approved / rejected /\n   replacement_requested -> expired``.\n- **Constraint**: exactly one target entity field must be set.\n- **Expired ribbon**: shown in the form view when the document has passed its\n   expiry date.\n\n``federation.compliance.check``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA check result linking a requirement to an entity's submission status.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Check title.\n- ``target_model`` (Selection): Entity type.\n- ``club_id`` / ``player_id`` / ``referee_id`` / ``venue_id`` /\n   ``club_representative_id`` (Many2one): Target.\n- ``status`` (Selection): ``compliant``, ``missing``, ``pending``, or\n   ``expired``.\n- ``requirement_id`` (Many2one): Requirement being checked.\n- ``submission_id`` (Many2one): Linked submission, when available.\n- ``checked_on`` (Datetime): Check timestamp.\n- ``note`` (Char): Result note.\n- ``target_display`` (Char, computed): Readable target name.\n\n``federation.compliance.check.archive``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nImmutable history row capturing how a compliance check looked at a point in\ntime.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``compliance_check_id`` (Many2one): Source compliance check.\n- ``archived_on`` / ``checked_on`` (Datetime): Archive timestamp and source\n   check timestamp.\n- ``target_model`` / ``target_res_id`` (Char / Integer): Archived target\n   reference.\n- ``requirement_id`` / ``submission_id`` (Many2one): Requirement and linked\n   submission snapshot.\n- ``status`` (Selection): Archived compliance status.\n- ``note`` (Char): Archived operator note.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Requirement definition**: federation staff define which documents each\n   entity type must provide.\n- **Submission workflow**: documents are uploaded, submitted, and reviewed with\n   approval or rejection outcomes.\n- **Expiry tracking**: computed ``is_expired`` flags overdue documents.\n- **Compliance checks**: programmatic checks produce compliant, missing,\n   pending, or expired statuses per entity.\n- **Multi-entity support**: the same framework covers clubs, players,\n   referees, venues, and club representatives.\n- **Portal self-service workspace**: scoped portal users can review their own\n   requirements, renewal deadlines, remediation notes, and submission history\n   at ``/my/compliance``.\n- **Portal submission flow**: club representatives and referees can upload\n   replacement documents and submit renewals directly from the portal detail\n   page without backend access. The controller delegates the write to\n   ``federation.document.submission._portal_submit_submission()`` so\n   attachment creation and submission state changes stay inside the model\n   boundary.\n- **Historical evidence**: compliance checks append archive rows on create and\n   on tracked status changes so operators can review how a target moved from\n   missing to compliant over time.\n\nPortal Self-Service\n-------------------\n\nPortal routes:\n\n- ``GET /my/compliance``: workspace listing with renewal warnings, review\n   state, and attention-first sorting.\n- ``GET /my/compliance/<requirement_id>/<target_model>/<target_id>``: detail\n   page for one requirement and target record.\n- ``POST /my/compliance/<requirement_id>/<target_model>/<target_id>/submit``:\n   attachment-backed submission or renewal request.\n\nPortal workspace behaviour:\n\n- Access is limited to targets the current portal user is allowed to manage.\n- Remediation notes from the reporting layer are surfaced when available.\n- Renewal windows are highlighted before expiry so replacement documents can be\n   submitted proactively.\n- Attachment creation preserves portal user identity while still using\n   controlled elevated writes through\n   ``_portal_submit_submission()`` and\n   ``_portal_create_submission_attachments()``.\n", "content_length": 6137, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_compliance/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "4817eb140f800f12ca9c5daf68004c3a269979bfb866470a7377d350c0a100c4", "size_bytes": 6137}

 {"content": "Sports Federation Import Tools\n==============================\n\nWizard-driven CSV import for clubs, seasons, teams, players, and tournament\nparticipants. The module is intended for federation onboarding and annual\nrollover work where administrators need rehearsable imports instead of raw ORM\nloads.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nThe import wizards provide a safer operator workflow than direct list imports:\n\n- dry-run rehearsal before any records are created\n- approval checkpoints before live imports execute\n- visible column mapping guidance in the wizard form\n- code-first reference lookup where the target models expose stable codes\n- categorized row-level failures instead of opaque batch errors\n- duplicate-safe behavior that reports and skips existing records\n- reusable template records that define the import contract per wizard\n- governance-job verification summaries with before/after target counts\n- managed partner contracts with token-authenticated subscriptions\n- staged inbound deliveries that reuse the same governed preview and approval\n  pipeline\n\nThe menu entry is available at ``Federation > Import Tools``.\nThe transient import models now live under the standard ``wizards/`` package to\nmatch the rest of the repository.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_base``: Clubs, seasons, teams.\n- ``sports_federation_people``: Players.\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournament participants.\n\nShared Wizard Behaviour\n-----------------------\n\nAll import wizards inherit ``federation.import.wizard.mixin``.\n\nShared capabilities:\n\n- UTF-8 and UTF-8 BOM CSV decoding.\n- Comma or semicolon delimiter support.\n- Reusable ``federation.import.template`` selection.\n- Checksum-bound ``federation.import.job`` approval workflow for live imports.\n- Shared fields: ``dry_run``, ``mapping_guide``, ``result_message``,\n  ``line_count``, ``success_count``, and ``error_count``.\n- Shared ``_execute_row_create(...)`` handling so live imports reuse one\n  row-create failure path instead of ad hoc wizard-level try/except blocks.\n- Standardized error categories such as ``missing_reference``,\n  ``duplicate_entry``, ``format_error``, and ``missing_required_field``.\n- Explicit compatibility handling for legacy CSV aliases tracked in\n  ``INTEGRATION_CONTRACTS.md``.\n\nManaged Partner Integrations\n----------------------------\n\nThe module also provides a managed integration layer for machine-driven import\nand export contracts.\n\nCore models:\n\n- ``federation.integration.contract`` defines the contract code, version,\n  direction, transport, route hint, availability requirements, and optional\n  linked import template.\n- ``federation.integration.partner`` stores partner identity, token rotation,\n  and delivery history.\n- ``federation.integration.partner.contract`` records which contracts a partner\n  is allowed to use.\n- ``federation.integration.delivery`` stages inbound partner payloads and links\n  them to the downstream governance job.\n\nCurrent model layout:\n\n- ``models/integration_contract.py`` keeps contract manifest and availability\n  rules.\n- ``models/integration_partner.py`` keeps partner identity, subscription\n  lookup, and the stable authentication entry point.\n- ``models/integration_partner_token_mixin.py`` keeps token generation,\n  hashing, verification, migration, and hashed persistence hooks.\n- ``models/integration_partner_rotation_mixin.py`` keeps manager-driven token\n  rotation and audit logging.\n- ``models/integration_partner_contract.py`` keeps subscription state and usage\n  tracking.\n- ``models/integration_delivery.py`` keeps the ORM fields and composes focused\n  helper mixins.\n- ``models/integration_delivery_stage_mixin.py`` keeps inbound staging,\n  idempotency, duplicate reuse, and attachment creation.\n- ``models/integration_delivery_workflow_mixin.py`` keeps wizard handoff and\n  delivery state transitions.\n- ``models/integration_delivery_retention_mixin.py`` keeps retention cleanup.\n\nCurrent wizard layout:\n\n- ``wizards/import_wizard_mixin.py`` remains the stable shared surface used by\n  all import wizards.\n- ``wizards/import_wizard_csv_mixin.py`` keeps CSV parsing, column validation,\n  row helpers, and shared error taxonomy.\n- ``wizards/import_wizard_governance_mixin.py`` keeps approval checks,\n  governance-job persistence, and result finalization.\n\nCurrent controller layout:\n\n- ``controllers/integration_api.py`` keeps the stable public route surface and\n  route-level orchestration.\n- ``controllers/integration_api_auth_mixin.py`` keeps header parsing, partner\n  authentication, caller identity, and rate-limit subject helpers.\n- ``controllers/integration_api_response_mixin.py`` keeps JSON response\n  shaping and typed error payload helpers.\n\nPhased Maintainability Plan\n---------------------------\n\n- Initial completed: the former multi-model gateway hotspot was split into\n  per-model files without changing model names, fields, or table ownership.\n  Test impact: existing import-tools tests should stay green. Migration risk:\n  none, because this is a file-layout change only.\n- Rules completed: delivery staging, idempotency, workflow handoff, and\n  retention cleanup now live in dedicated helper mixins while\n  ``federation.integration.delivery`` keeps the ORM contract stable. Test\n  impact: inbound delivery staging, idempotency, and retention coverage stays\n  green. Migration risk: replay semantics and attachment linkage.\n- Integration completed: token generation, hashing, verification, migration, and\n  rotation or audit helpers now live in dedicated partner mixins while\n  ``federation.integration.partner`` keeps the stable ORM entry points for\n  authentication and subscription lookup. Test impact: token rotation and\n  legacy-token migration coverage stay green. Migration risk: stored hash\n  compatibility and audit logging.\n- API completed: ``wizards/import_wizard_mixin.py`` now composes dedicated\n  CSV and governance or result helper mixins while preserving the shared wizard\n  API. Test impact: shared mixin coverage plus wizard-specific dry-run and\n  live-import flows stay green. Migration risk: approval checksum binding and\n  result-summary compatibility.\n- Operations completed: ``controllers/integration_api.py`` now composes dedicated\n  auth and response helper mixins while preserving the public route surface and\n  existing headers and status codes. Test impact: integration API credential,\n  rate-limit, finance export, and inbound delivery coverage stays green.\n  Migration risk: request patching in tests and route-level error semantics.\n\nManaged Integration Behaviour\n-----------------------------\n\n- Authentication: partners use ``X-Federation-Partner-Code`` plus either\n  ``X-Federation-Partner-Token`` or ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``.\n- Contract manifest: ``/integration/v1/contracts`` exposes the subscribed\n  contract manifest, including database-specific availability and deprecation\n  metadata.\n- Inbound deliveries: ``/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries``\n  stores staged deliveries with checksum-based duplicate reuse and can bind an\n  ``X-Federation-Idempotency-Key`` for safe retries.\n- Operator workflow: operators open the staged delivery directly in the\n  matching import wizard, review the preview, request approval, and then run\n  the live import.\n- Auditability: delivery records mirror preview, approval, completion, and\n  failure states so the inbound handoff remains auditable.\n\nManaged Integration Contract Docs\n---------------------------------\n\n- Narrative policy and deprecation guidance live in\n  ``INTEGRATION_CONTRACTS.md``.\n- Machine-readable route and payload definitions live in\n  ``openapi/integration_v1.yaml``.\n- Partner onboarding golden examples live in\n  ``openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md``.\n\nCorrelation ID Standard\n-----------------------\n\n- Managed integration routes accept optional\n  ``X-Federation-Correlation-Id`` headers.\n- JSON responses include ``correlation_id`` and mirror it in the\n  ``X-Federation-Correlation-Id`` response header.\n- CSV exports include ``X-Federation-Correlation-Id`` for cross-service\n  traceability.\n- Typed JSON error payloads include ``error``, ``error_code``, and\n  ``correlation_id``.\n\nCredential Handling\n-------------------\n\n- Partner secrets are stored hashed at rest; the raw token is never shown\n  again after issuance.\n- Federation managers issue or rotate a token from the partner form, then copy\n  it from the one-time modal.\n- Each manager-driven token rotation writes a shared audit event that appears\n  in ``Reporting > Token Rotation Audit``.\n- URL query parameters are rejected for partner authentication to avoid\n  leaking secrets into logs, browser history, or proxy traces.\n- Legacy plaintext tokens are migrated into hashed storage on module load and\n  flagged for mandatory rotation.\n\nInbound Delivery Guardrails\n---------------------------\n\n- Partner uploads must use a ``.csv`` filename and a ``text/csv`` content type\n  when declared.\n- Inbound payloads larger than 5 MiB are rejected before staging.\n- Duplicate inbound payloads are deduplicated by checksum before a new\n  delivery record or attachment is created.\n- Explicit inbound idempotency keys replay the original delivery across\n  retries and reject conflicting payload reuse.\n- Successful inbound API responses expose ``delivery_outcome`` plus\n  ``X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome`` so clients can distinguish fresh staging\n  from checksum reuse and idempotent replay.\n- Terminal inbound deliveries are purged automatically once they exceed the\n  retention windows documented in ``DATA_RETENTION_POLICY.md``; the staged\n  payload attachment is deleted with the delivery record.\n\nSupported Wizards\n-----------------\n\n``federation.import.clubs.wizard``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nRequired columns:\n\n- ``name``\n\nRecommended columns:\n\n- ``code``, ``email``, ``phone``, ``city``\n\nDuplicate matching:\n\n- ``code`` first, then exact club ``name``\n\n``federation.import.seasons.wizard``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nRequired columns:\n\n- ``name``, ``code``, ``date_start``, ``date_end``\n\nOptional columns:\n\n- ``state``, ``notes``, ``target_club_count``, ``target_team_count``,\n  ``target_tournament_count``, ``target_participant_count``\n\nValidation notes:\n\n- Dates must use ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\n- State must be one of ``draft``, ``open``, ``closed``, or ``cancelled``.\n- Planning target columns must be whole numbers greater than or equal to zero.\n\n``federation.import.teams.wizard``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nRequired columns:\n\n- ``team_name`` or ``name``\n- ``club_code`` or ``club_name``\n\nRecommended columns:\n\n- ``code``, ``category``, ``gender``, ``email``, ``phone``\n\nDuplicate matching:\n\n- ``code`` first, then ``(club_id, name)``\n\n``federation.import.players.wizard``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nRequired columns:\n\n- ``first_name`` and ``last_name``\n- Legacy imports may use ``name`` when it contains  {"content": "# Competition Registration\n\nThe Registration Desk manages team entries for a competition edition and division.\n\n## Team selection\n\nWhen creating or editing a competition entry, the team dropdown is limited to:\n\n- active teams;\n- teams eligible for the selected division's category and gender;\n- teams that are not already entered in the same registration window.\n\nThe available-team list is computed per division and the form applies it as a\nselection domain. The model also validates the same rules on create and write,\nso direct ORM or API requests cannot bypass the desk filter. Changing a window\nclears an existing team selection when it is no longer valid.\n\nEligibility uses the tournament module's existing `search_eligible_teams()` and\n`get_team_eligibility_error()` APIs. No historical registration entries are\nrewritten by this filtering; it only affects new selections and invalid direct\nwrites.\n\n## Regression tests\n\nThe regression coverage is in\n`tests/test_registration_team_selection.py`. Run it with the repository's\nmodule-level Odoo test workflow after installing the registration addon and its\ndeclared dependencies.\n", "content_length": 1135, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_registration/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "c0496e6d758dc7652fceb59fc8f9678fe35c7b4bc86a5389a9b3cbafc5b1ba0f", "size_bytes": 1135}

 {"content": "# Sports Federation Reporting\n\nCross-module analytical reports backed by PostgreSQL views plus scheduled report\nsnapshots. Provides read-only report models that aggregate participation,\nofficiating, compliance, finance, and tournament-readiness data into\noperator-facing views.\n\n## Purpose\n\nGives federation administrators a **dashboard-level view** of key metrics without\nwriting SQL or building custom reports. Each report model is a database view\nthat joins and aggregates data from multiple modules into a single, filterable\nlist or pivot view, while report schedules generate recurring weekly or monthly\nCSV snapshots from inside Odoo.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs, teams, seasons |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Players |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournaments |\n| `sports_federation_officiating` | Referees, assignments |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings data |\n| `sports_federation_discipline` | Disciplinary data |\n| `sports_federation_compliance` | Compliance data |\n| `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | Finance events |\n| `sports_federation_import_tools` | Inbound delivery failures for operator checklist reporting |\n\nAudit dashboard surfaces:\n\n- `Reporting > Portal Audit` groups privileged portal create/write/call activity\n\temitted through `federation.portal.privilege`.\n- `Reporting > Token Rotation Audit` groups manager-driven integration partner\n\ttoken rotation events emitted from the import-tools token rotation flow.\n- both dashboards read the shared `federation.audit.event` log so additional\n\taudited workflows can reuse the same reporting contract later.\n\n## Models (all SQL view-backed, `_auto = False`)\n\n### `federation.report.participation`\n\nClub participation summary per season.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Season |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Club |\n| `team_count` | Integer | Teams registered |\n| `player_count` | Integer | Players licensed |\n| `tournament_count` | Integer | Tournaments entered |\n\n### `federation.report.officiating`\n\nReferee workload summary.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `referee_id` | Many2one | Referee |\n| `certification_level` | Char | Current level |\n| `assignment_count` | Integer | Total assignments |\n| `completed_assignment_count` | Integer | Completed assignments |\n\n### `federation.report.compliance`\n\nCompliance status overview by entity type.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `target_model` | Char | Entity type |\n| `compliant_count` | Integer | Entities in compliance |\n| `missing_count` | Integer | Missing documents |\n| `pending_count` | Integer | Awaiting review |\n| `expired_count` | Integer | Expired documents |\n| `non_compliant_count` | Integer | Explicitly rejected or non-compliant checks |\n\n### `federation.report.finance`\n\nFinancial event summary by fee type and state.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `fee_type_id` | Many2one | Fee category |\n| `state` | Selection | Event state |\n| `event_count` | Integer | Number of events |\n| `total_amount` | Float | Sum of amounts |\n\n### `federation.report.operational`\n\nTournament-level operational KPI view.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` / `tournament_id` | Many2one | Scope of the `completed_match_count` | Integer | Match execution totals |\n| `match_completion_rate` | Float | Completed-match percentage |\n| `pending_finance_event_count` / `pending_finance_amount` | Integer / `healthy`, `attention`, or `blocked` |\n| `readiness_note` | Text | Operator-readable summary of the active readiness blockers or follow-up work |\n\n### `blocked` |\n| `summary` | Text | Operator-readable explanation of what the queue means |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Read-only views** — Analytical models use `_auto = False` with `init()` creating SQL views.\n2. **Role-oriented reporting surfaces** — Operational KPIs, standings reconciliation, finance reconciliation, and compliance summaries are separated into task-specific menus instead of a single generic export path.\n3. **Cross-module joins** — Operational KPIs combine tournament, standings, finance, and compliance data into one application-layer view.\n4. **Recurring snapshots** — `federation.report.schedule` can generate weekly or monthly CSV snapshots and a daily cron refreshes active schedules.\n5. **Reconciliation-first reporting** — Standings coverage, finance follow-up, failed-notification queues, missing discipline-finance events, and stalled workflow queues expose the specific gaps operators must resolve before relying on downstream outputs.\n6. **Season operations checklist** — The reporting layer now includes a season-level checklist that surfaces review queues, publication gaps, and unresolved workflow exceptions in one place.\n7. **Planning decision support** — Season portfolio and club performance views turn the reporting layer into a planning and delivery-monitoring surface instead of a pure export utility.\n8. **Legacy CSV exports preserved** — The lightweight HTTP CSV endpoints remain available for ad hoc export use.\n9. **Contract-tagged exports** — Authenticated CSV responses now include explicit contract and version headers for downstream consumers.\n10. **Operator checklist** — Notification failures, workflow exceptions, finance follow-up, inbound delivery failures, blocked season readiness, and scheduled report failures now surface in one menu.\n11. **Persistent schedule failure tracking** — Report schedules keep the last failure timestamp, error message, and consecutive failure count so recurring problems survive beyond transient logs.\n12. **Generated-file retention** — Scheduled report artifacts are cleared automatically after the retention window in `DATA_RETENTION_POLICY.md`, while the schedule metadata and next run remain intact.\n\n## CSV exports\n\nAuthenticated backend users can export lightweight KPI CSV files from the\nreporting controllers:\n\n- `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>` — standings lines with tie-break notes\n- `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>` — season participation roster\n- `/reporting/export/finance` — finance summary grouped by fee type and state\n- `/reporting/export/finance/events` — detailed finance-event handoff export with reconciliation references and closure timestamps\n\nEach export now exposes `X-Federation-Contract` and\n`X-Federation-Contract-Version` headers. -{"content": "# Schedule Approval\n\nThis addon owns independent schedule review and immutable schedule publication.\nIt does not own working assignments, calendar capacity, or match-day execution.\n\n## Operator flow\n\n1. A schedule planner submits a complete schedule from **Schedule Planner**.\n2. The addon creates immutable review evidence and opens the pending review.\n3. A different assigned schedule approver opens **Schedule Review Queue**.\n4. The approver either enters a note and selects **Request Changes**, or selects\n   **Approve Schedule**.\n5. Operational match links are derived and may be materialized at\npublication. Buttons are only orchestration entry points and never duplicate\nthe business rules.\nRole assignments remain administrator-managed; the Schedule Approver group\nexposes the workflow actions, while a per-edition `schedule_approver` assignment\nauthorizes the operation. The role check performs a read-only internal lookup,\nand approval revalidation performs controlled read-only access to the submitted\ncalendar and venue data, so approvers do not need CRUD access to those\nadministrator-managed records. +{"content": "# Schedule Approval\n\nThis addon owns independent schedule review and immutable schedule publication.\nIt does not own working assignments, calendar capacity, or match-day execution.\n\n## Operator flow\n\n1. A schedule planner submits a complete schedule from **Schedule Planner**.\n2. The addon creates immutable review evidence and opens the pending review.\n3. A different assigned schedule approver opens **Schedule Review Queue**.\n4. The approver either enters a note and selects **Request Changes**, or selects\n   **Approve Schedule**.\n5. Approved reviews appear under **Publication > Approved Schedules**.\n6. **Publish Schedule** creates any missing operational matches for the assigned\n   fixtures through the fixture materializer, creates an immutable publication,\n   links matches to their exact slots, and makes the publication current for the\n   match day.\n7. **Publication > Schedule Publications** retains live and superseded evidence.\n\nThe command service enforces edition roles, separation of duties, submitted\nrevision equality, snapshot-digest equality for schedule facts, and schedule\nrevalidation. Operational match links are derived and may be materialized at\npublication. Buttons are only orchestration entry points and never duplicate\nthe business rules.\nEach review records the authenticated schedule planner who submits it, so that\nplanner can withdraw a pending review before an approver decides it.\nRole assignments remain administrator-managed; the Schedule Approver group\nexposes the workflow actions, while a per-edition `schedule_approver` assignment\nauthorizes the operation. The role check performs a read-only internal lookup,\nand approval revalidation performs controlled read-only access to the submitted\ncalendar and venue data, so approvers do not need CRUD access to those\nadministrator-managed records. Reviewers may edit the note while a review is\npending; state and audit fields remain command-service-only.\n\n## Tests and contracts\n\n```bash\npython ci/check_competition_pipeline_contract.py\npython ci/check_schedule_handoff_contract.py\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_schedule_approval\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n```\n\n## 5.1.1 integrity rules\n\nReview evidence is immutable through the model guard. +FILE: ci/capture_migration_invariants.py

+SHA256: c0142aed5dffe8034c35151678ea16713c9c093ba3e7a533c1c25803cd953ab4

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Capture release migration counts and integrity checks from PostgreSQL."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+DEFAULT_CONTRACT = ROOT / "ci/release_invariants.json"
+
+
+def run_sql(database: str, sql: str) -> int:
+    command = [
+        "psql",
+        "--host", os.environ.get("PGHOST", "127.0.0.1"),
+        "--port", os.environ.get("PGPORT", "5432"),
+        "--username", os.environ.get("PGUSER", "odoo"),
+        "--dbname", database,
+        "--tuples-only",
+        "--no-align",
+        "--set", "ON_ERROR_STOP=1",
+        "--command", sql,
+    ]
+    result = subprocess.run(
+        command,
+        check=False,
+        text=True,
+        capture_output=True,
+        env={**os.environ, "PGPASSWORD": os.environ.get("PGPASSWORD", "odoo")},
+    )
+    if result.returncode:
+        raise RuntimeError(result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip())
+    value = result.stdout.strip()
+    try:
+        return int(value)
+    except ValueError as error:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"Invariant query did not return an integer: {value!r}") from error
+
+
+def validate_contract(contract: dict) -> None:
+    if contract.get("schema_version") != 1:
+        raise ValueError("Invariant contract schema_version must be 1")
+    for section in ("counts", "zero_checks"):
+        entries = contract.get(section)
+        if not isinstance(entries, dict) or not entries:
+            raise ValueError(f"Invariant contract {section} must be a non-empty object")
+        for name, query in entries.items():
+            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name.strip():
+                raise ValueError(f"Invariant contract {section} has an empty name")
+            if not isinstance(query, str) or not query.lstrip().upper().startswith("SELECT"):
+                raise ValueError(f"Invariant {name!r} must be a SELECT query")
+    modes = contract.get("count_modes", {})
+    unknown_modes = set(modes) - set(contract["counts"])
+    if unknown_modes:
+        raise ValueError(f"Count modes reference unknown counts: {sorted(unknown_modes)}")
+    for name in contract["counts"]:
+        if modes.get(name, "exact") not in {"exact", "minimum"}:
+            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported count mode for {name!r}")
+
+
+def capture(database: str, contract: dict) -> dict:
+    return {
+        "schema_version": 1,
+        "captured_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
+        "database": database,
+        "count_modes": {
+            name: contract.get("count_modes", {}).get(name, "exact")
+            for name in sorted(contract["counts"])
+        },
+        "counts": {
+            name: run_sql(database, query)
+            for name, query in sorted(contract["counts"].items())
+        },
+        "zero_checks": {
+            name: run_sql(database, query)
+            for name, query in sorted(contract["zero_checks"].items())
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--database", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--contract", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_CONTRACT)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    try:
+        contract = json.loads(args.contract.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+        validate_contract(contract)
+        evidence = capture(args.database, contract)
+    except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
+        print(f"Migration invariant capture failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(evidence, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    print(args.output)
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
+

+FILE: ci/compare_migration_invariants.py
+SIZE: 3044
+CONTENT-LENGTH: 3044
+SHA256: ebf0c95f11463fa7c3d37f546d0f8e9a9553c297a016a1b31619d202d5a0e115
+GIT-MODE: 100755
+FILESYSTEM-MODE: 0755

+====================================================================================================
+
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Compare pre-upgrade, post-upgrade, and rollback invariant evidence."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import sys
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def load(path: Path) -> dict:
+    payload = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+    if payload.get("schema_version") != 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported invariant evidence schema in {path}")
+    return payload
+
+
+def compare(
+    reference: dict,
+    candidate: dict,
+    label: str,
+    *,
+    force_exact: bool = False,
+) -> list[dict]:
+    differences = []
+    modes = reference.get("count_modes", {})
+    for name, expected in sorted(reference.get("counts", {}).items()):
+        actual = candidate.get("counts", {}).get(name)
+        mode = "exact" if force_exact else modes.get(name, "exact")
+        violates = actual is None or (actual != expected if mode == "exact" else actual < expected)
+        if violates:
+            differences.append(
+                {
+                    "kind": "count",
+                    "name": name,
+                    "mode": mode,
+                    "expected": expected,
+                    "actual": actual,
+                    "evidence": label,
+                }
+            )
+    for name, actual in sorted(candidate.get("zero_checks", {}).items()):
+        if actual != 0:
+            differences.append(
+                {"kind": "integrity", "name": name, "expected": 0, "actual": actual, "evidence": label}
+            )
+    return differences
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--before", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--after", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--rollback", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, required=True)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    try:
+        before = load(args.before)
+        after = load(args.after)
+        differences = compare(before, after, "after")
+        rollback = load(args.rollback) if args.rollback else None
+        if rollback:
+            differences.extend(compare(before, rollback, "rollback", force_exact=True))
+    except (OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
+        print(f"Migration invariant comparison failed: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    result = {
+        "schema_version": 1,
+        "compared_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
+        "status": "passed" if not differences else "failed",
+        "before": str(args.before),
+        "after": str(args.after),
+        "rollback": str(args.rollback) if args.rollback else None,
+        "differences": differences,
+    }
+    args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    args.output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
+    if differences:
+        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, sort_keys=True), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    print(args.output)
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
+

+import logging
+from datetime import timedelta
+
+from odoo import _, api, fields, models
+from odoo.exceptions import UserError, ValidationError
+
+_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+class FederationOperationJob(models.Model):
+    _name = "federation.operation.job"
+    _description = "Operational Job"
+    _order = "priority desc, requested_on asc, id asc"
+
+    state = fields.Selection(
+        [
+            ("pending", "Pending"),
+            ("running", "Running"),
+            ("retry", "Retry Scheduled"),
+            ("done", "Done"),
+            ("operator_action", "Needs Operator Action"),
+        ],
+        default="pending",
+        required=True,
+        index=True,
+    )
+    name = fields.Char(required=True)
+    source_model = fields.Char(required=True, index=True)
+    source_res_id = fields.Integer(required=True, index=True)
+    correlation_id = fields.Char(required=True, index=True)
+    priority = fields.Integer(default=50, index=True)
+    requested_on = fields.Datetime(default=fields.Datetime.now, required=True, index=True)
+    started_on = fields.Datetime(index=True)
+    completed_on = fields.Datetime(index=True)
+    next_retry_on = fields.Datetime(index=True)
+    operator_action_on = fields.Datetime(index=True)
+    attempt_count = fields.Integer(default=0, required=True)
+    max_attempts = fields.Integer(default=3, required=True)
+    last_error = fields.Text(readonly=True)
+    failure_category = fields.Char(index=True, readonly=True)
+
+    _unique_source_correlation = models.Constraint(
+        "unique(source_model, source_res_id, correlation_id)",
+        "A source record can have only one job for a correlation ID.",
+    )
+
+    @api.constrains("attempt_count", "max_attempts")
+    def _check_attempts(self):
+        for job in self:
+            if job.attempt_count < 0 or job.max_attempts < 1:
+                raise ValidationError(_("Job attempt limits are invalid."))
+
+    @api.model
+    def ensure_job(self, source, correlation_id, name=False, max_attempts=3, priority=50):
+        source.ensure_one()
+        values = {
+            "name": name or source.display_name,
+            "source_model": source._name,
+            "source_res_id": source.id,
+            "correlation_id": correlation_id,
+            "max_attempts": max_attempts,
+            "priority": priority,
+        }
+        job = self.search(
+            [
+                ("source_model", "=", source._name),
+                ("source_res_id", "=", source.id),
+                ("correlation_id", "=", correlation_id),
+            ],
+            limit=1,
+        )
+        return job or self.create(values)
+
+    def _source(self):
+        self.ensure_one()
+        model = self.env.get(self.source_model)
+        return model.browse(self.source_res_id).exists() if model is not None else model
+
+    def _start(self):
+        self.ensure_one()
+        self.write(
+            {
+                "state": "running",
+                "started_on": fields.Datetime.now(),
+                "completed_on": False,
+                "next_retry_on": False,
+                "attempt_count": self.attempt_count + 1,
+            }
+        )
+
+    def _succeed(self):
+        self.write(
+            {
+                "state": "done",
+                "completed_on": fields.Datetime.now(),
+                "next_retry_on": False,
+                "operator_action_on": False,
+                "last_error": False,
+                "failure_category": False,
+            }
+        )
+
+    def _fail(self, error, category="unexpected_bug", retryable=True):
+        self.ensure_one()
+        exhausted = self.attempt_count >= self.max_attempts or not retryable
+        delay_minutes = min(60, 2 ** max(1, self.attempt_count))
+        self.write(
+            {
+                "state": "operator_action" if exhausted else "retry",
+                "completed_on": fields.Datetime.now(),
+                "next_retry_on": False if exhausted else fields.Datetime.now() + timedelta(minutes=delay_minutes),
+                "operator_action_on": fields.Datetime.now() if exhausted else False,
+                "last_error": str(error)[:4000],
+                "failure_category": category,
+            }
+        )
+
+    def _execute(self):
+        self.ensure_one()
+        source = self._source()
+        if not source:
+            self._fail(_("The source record no longer exists."), "data_validation", retryable=False)
+            return False
+        self._start()
+        try:
+            source.with_context(federation_correlation_id=self.correlation_id)._retry_operational_job(self)
+        except Exception as error:  # pylint: disable=broad-except
+            retryable = not isinstance(error, (UserError, ValidationError))
+            self._fail(error, "unexpected_bug", retryable=retryable)
+            _logger.exception("Operational job failed: job=%s correlation_id=%s", self.id, self.correlation_id)
+            return False
+        self._succeed()
+        return True
+
+    def action_retry(self):
+        for job in self:
+            if job.state not in ("retry", "operator_action"):
+                raise ValidationError(_("Only failed jobs can be retried."))
+            job.write(
+                {
+                    "state": "pending",
+                    "attempt_count": 0,
+                    "next_retry_on": False,
+                    "operator_action_on": False,
+                }
+            )
+        return True
+
+    def action_open_source(self):
+        self.ensure_one()
+        source = self._source()
+        if not source:
+            raise UserError(_("The source record no longer exists."))
+        return {
+            "type": "ir.actions.act_window",
+            "res_model": source._name,
+            "res_id": source.id,
+            "view_mode": "form",
+            "target": "current",
+        }
+
+    @api.model
+    def _recover_stale(self, stale_minutes=30):
+        deadline = fields.Datetime.now() - timedelta(minutes=stale_minutes)
+        stale = self.search([("state", "=", "running"), ("started_on", "<=", deadline)])
+        for job in stale:
+            job._fail(_("Recovered after the worker stopped while processing."), "infrastructure")
+        return len(stale)
+
+    @api.model
+    def _cron_process_jobs(self):
+        self._recover_stale()
+        jobs = self.search(
+            [
+                ("state", "in", ("pending", "retry")),
+                "|",
+                ("next_retry_on", "=", False),
+                ("next_retry_on", "<=", fields.Datetime.now()),
+            ],
+            order="priority desc, requested_on asc, id asc",
+            limit=50,
+        )
+        return sum(1 for job in jobs if job._execute())
+

+class FederationRetentionPolicy(models.Model):
+    _name = "federation.retention.policy"
+    _description = "Retention Policy Health"
+    _order = "name"
+
+    name = fields.Char(required=True, translate=True)
+    code = fields.Char(required=True, index=True)
+    source_model = fields.Char(required=True)
+    active = fields.Boolean(default=True)
+    expected_interval_hours = fields.Integer(default=24, required=True)
+    policy_version = fields.Char(default="1", required=True)
+    latest_evidence_id = fields.Many2one("federation.retention.evidence", compute="_compute_health")
+    latest_success_on = fields.Datetime(compute="_compute_health")
+    health = fields.Selection([("healthy", "Healthy"), ("attention", "Attention"), ("overdue", "Overdue"), ("never_run", "Never Run")], compute="_compute_health", search="_search_health")
+    health_message = fields.Char(compute="_compute_health")
+    _unique_code = models.Constraint("unique(code)", "Retention policy codes must be unique.")
+
+    @api.constrains("expected_interval_hours")
+    def _check_expected_interval(self):
+        if any(policy.expected_interval_hours < 1 for policy in self):
+            raise ValidationError(_("Expected retention intervals must be positive."))
+
+    def _compute_health(self):
+        now = fields.Datetime.now()
+        Evidence = self.env["federation.retention.evidence"].sudo()
+        for policy in self:
+            latest = Evidence.search([("policy", "=", policy.code)], order="completed_on desc,id desc", limit=1)
+            latest_success = Evidence.search([("policy", "=", policy.code), ("status", "=", "passed")], order="completed_on desc,id desc", limit=1)
+            policy.latest_evidence_id = latest
+            policy.latest_success_on = latest_success.completed_on
+            if not latest:
+                policy.health = "never_run"; policy.health_message = _("No execution evidence has been recorded.")
+            elif latest.status == "failed":
+                policy.health = "attention"; policy.health_message = latest.operator_message or _("The latest retention execution failed.")
+            elif (now - latest.completed_on).total_seconds() / 3600 > policy.expected_interval_hours:
+                policy.health = "overdue"; policy.health_message = _("No successful execution within the expected interval.")
+            elif latest.skipped_count or latest.failure_count:
+                policy.health = "attention"; policy.health_message = _("The latest execution completed with skipped records or failures.")
+            else:
+                policy.health = "healthy"; policy.health_message = _("The latest execution completed successfully.")
+
+    @api.model
+    def _search_health(self, operator, value):
+        policies = self.search([])
+        if operator in ("=", "=="): matched = policies.filtered(lambda policy: policy.health == value)
+        elif operator == "in": matched = policies.filtered(lambda policy: policy.health in value)
+        elif operator in ("!=", "<>"): matched = policies.filtered(lambda policy: policy.health != value)
+        elif operator == "not in": matched = policies.filtered(lambda policy: policy.health not in value)
+        else: raise ValidationError(_("Unsupported retention health search operator."))
+        return [("id", "in", matched.ids)]
+
+    def action_open_evidence(self):

+        action = self.env["ir.actions.actions"]._for_xml_id("sports_federation_base.action_federation_retention_evidence")
+        action["domain"] = [("policy", "=", self.code)]
+        return action

+from datetime import timedelta
+
+from odoo import fields
+from odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase
+
+
+class TestOperationJob(TransactionCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        super().setUp()
+        source = self.env["res.partner"].create({"name": "Job Source"})
+        self.job = self.env["federation.operation.job"].create({
+            "name": "Test Job", "source_model": source._name,
+            "source_res_id": source.id, "correlation_id": "job-test-1",
+            "max_attempts": 2,
+        })
+
+    def test_failure_uses_backoff_then_operator_action(self):
+        self.job._start(); self.job._fail("temporary")
+        self.assertEqual(self.job.state, "retry")
+        self.assertTrue(self.job.next_retry_on)
+        self.job._start(); self.job._fail("still broken")
+        self.assertEqual(self.job.state, "operator_action")
+        self.assertFalse(self.job.next_retry_on)
+
+    def test_manual_retry_resets_terminal_job(self):
+        self.job.write({"state": "operator_action", "attempt_count": 2})
+        self.job.action_retry()
+        self.assertEqual(self.job.state, "pending")
+        self.assertEqual(self.job.attempt_count, 0)
+
+    def test_stale_running_job_is_recovered(self):
+        self.job.write({"state": "running", "attempt_count": 1,
+                        "started_on": fields.Datetime.now() - timedelta(hours=1)})
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(self.env["federation.operation.job"]._recover_stale(), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(self.job.state, "retry")
